messages:
jamie: Heads-up — since 10:12 UTC we've been getting high 429 rate and token/s SLO alerts for the Nimbus dedicated pool. Traffic looks bursty after a campaign.
roberto: Can you paste the pool id + sample admission logs?
jamie: pool=nimbus-prod-pool, tenant_id=acct-NIMB. Here's the admission controller tail (just the interesting lines):
```
2026-03-17T10:12:03Z admission: reject tenant=acct-NIMB reason=burst_credits_exhausted used=12000 remaining=0 window=60s
2026-03-17T10:12:05Z admission: throttle tenant=acct-NIMB reason=admission_headroom breach=85%
2026-03-17T10:12:31Z proxy: upstream_latency=1.2s status=200 tokens=320
2026-03-17T10:12:45Z admission: reject tenant=acct-OTHER reason=quota_fairness enforced
```
jamie: Also saw billing accounting spikes (credits decreased faster than expected).
anya: Pinging eng-runtime-oncall to triage noisy neighbor vs billing mismatch. @eng-runtime-oncall can you take a look? :eyes:
eng-runtime-oncall: On it — pulling metrics for that pool now. Which autoscale group is attached?
jamie: autoscale_group=nimbus-prod-asg-7. Recent deploy 03/15 changed batching config to prefer latency. Not sure if that affects token draw.
marcel: I'm looking at admission metrics — per-tenant burst credits dropped to zero around 10:11:50. But aggregate pool headroom still had ~20% capacity. Suggests per-tenant accounting (burst token bucket) is the limiter.
roberto: Could be two issues: 1) a noisy tenant legitimately exhausted credits, 2) token meter bug double-counting on retries. Any signs of double-counting?
marcel: Check proxy retry logs. If retries increment token counters for the same request path, that would double-burn.
jamie: grep'ed retried requests; saw a few 502->retry loops at 10:09-10:11. Example: `internal-proxy: retry attempt=1 upstream=runtime-23 status=502 request_id=rid-8a2`.
anya: Quick mitigation options: 1) emergency top-up of tenant burst credits, 2) relax admission headroom threshold from 15% to 10% for this pool, 3) temp route traffic to fallback-compatible model variant. Which do we want first?
roberto: Do 1 + 2 in parallel. Top-up so customer doesn't see 429s. Relax headroom to avoid immediate rejections while we investigate. Use the CLI: `ri-cli billing adjust-burst --tenant acct-NIMB --add 50000` and `ri-cli admission update --pool nimbus-prod-pool --headroom 10`.
jamie: Running the CLI now.
jamie: ```
$ ri-cli billing adjust-burst --tenant acct-NIMB --add 50000
> success: new_burst_balance=50000
$ ri-cli admission update --pool nimbus-prod-pool --headroom 10
> success: headroom=10%
```
support-bot: Alert suppressed for acct-NIMB for 30m per manual mitigation.
roberto: After top-up + headroom tweak, are 429 rates falling?
eng-runtime-oncall: Early signs yes — 429s decreased from 18% -> 3% in the last 5m. Latency still elevated for some requests.
marcel: Elevated latency correlates with retries between proxy <-> runtime. Let's throttle retries temporarily: `proxy-config set retry.max_attempts=1` for the pool.
anya: Proceeding with retry change (1 attempt) and enabling verbose tracing for 10m.
jamie: Done. Re-checking logs, proxy retry loops stopped. Latency median dropped from 750ms to 210ms.
roberto: Good. Now root cause investigation items: 1) audit token-meter paths to ensure retries don't double-burn credits, 2) reconcile billing ledger vs admission counters for acct-NIMB to see timing deltas, 3) evaluate whether recent batching config changed observed token draw per request.
marcel: I'll open an eng-runtime ticket and attach perf traces. Provisional bug: `token_meter:increment` invoked in both proxy and runtime on retry success.
roberto: Owners: marcel (eng-runtime), anya (sre), jamie (support/customer liaison).
jamie: I'll message the customer that we've applied an emergency top-up + mitigations and we're investigating root cause; will follow up with timeline. :white_check_mark:
eng-runtime-oncall: Filing incident note and linking traces: https://console.redwood/trace/trace-2378 (internal).
roberto: Next actions: - marcel: reproduce double-count scenario in staging and write fix for meter idempotency - anya: billing reconciliation and confirm if ledger adjustments needed - jamie: coordinate customer comms and confirm if they want permanent increased burst allowance
jamie: Customer replied: "Thanks, seeing much fewer 429s. We'll take the increased allowance for 24h while you investigate."
marcel: Repro steps I'm using in staging (sharing so SREs can validate):
```bash
# simulate token/s burst to exhaust per-tenant bucket
wrk -t12 -c200 -d120s -s scripts/hotloop.lua --latency http://nimbus-staging.internal/generate
# watch admission logs
tail -f /var/log/redwood/admission.log | rg acct-STAGE-NIMB
```
roberto: Nice. Also run with `--trace-headers` to capture request IDs so meter calls can be cross-checked.
anya: Leaving follow-up alert that will fire if per-tenant burst credits go below 5k again.
jamie: Closing the support escalation for now — customer stable, mitigations applied. Will reopen if billing reconciliation requires customer billing correction. :thumbsup:
marcel: I'll push a hotfix branch to prevent double-increment on retries and request a canary deploy.
roberto: Thanks team. Postmortem to follow (include timeline, mitigations, and recommended policy changes: conservative batching rollback and per-tenant rollout limits).
support-bot: Thread archived after 2h inactivity.
